prompt:
Write 6 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a side impact at intersection claim, in time order. Injury: knee injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1025; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- It is not yet clear whether the injury came from this crash.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Nothing independent confirms the accident: no witnesses, no photos and no other report.
- The damage does not match the story: the dents are on another side and at another height than the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver lives with the policyholder and is covered as a household member.
text:
Entry 1: Claim reported by the claimant following a side impact at an intersection. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer, and a knee injury is listed on the first notice of loss.

Entry 2: Reviewed the claimant's account of the collision, which was consistent across each conversation held so far. Police records and a witness statement confirm the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of the crash.

Entry 3: Inspected the vehicle photos supplied by the repair shop. The dents sit on the opposite side of the car and at a different height from the impact described, so the damage pattern does not match the account given. No earlier damage to the vehicle is known, and nothing suggests the damage predates the start of coverage.

Entry 4: Nothing independent confirms the accident itself. There are no witnesses beyond those already noted, no photos from the scene, and no other report on file. The driver is a member of the policyholder's household and is covered as such.

Entry 5: Medical records show a course of treatment for the knee that followed a usual pattern and tapered off as the patient improved. No earlier injury to the same area is known. It is still unclear whether this injury was caused by the crash.

Entry 6: Next step is to request the full medical file and the repair estimate, then reassess causation of the knee injury and the mismatch in damage before any decision on the claim.
